title: Offline deployment verification and migration playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for performing offline (air-gapped) installs and controlled version migrations of Redwood Private clusters. It focuses on verification, idempotent migration steps, and small automation scripts operators can run in environments without outbound access. The goal is a repeatable preflight -> mirror -> consume -> upgrade -> verify flow with clear rollback gates.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: VPC/on-prem Redwood Private deployments using our Kubernetes operator + infra TF modules.
- Assumes an administrative bastion or jump host inside the customer network that can receive artifacts via removable media (USB/tape) or an internal jump-transfer service.
- Assumes access to customer internal registry (Harbor/Azure ACR Airgap mode/Artifactory) that will act as the offline registry.
- Assumes TLS certs and KMS/hardware HSM for keystore are provisioned by customer (playbook includes integration notes, not cert issuance).

High-level flow (one-line):
1) Preflight checks -> 2) Artifact capture & signing -> 3) Import to offline registry -> 4) TF state & infra plan (dry run) -> 5) Apply operator and platform upgrades canary -> 6) Run verification suites -> 7) Final rollout or rollback.

1) PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (local to bastion)
- Confirm inventory: list of nodes, k8s versions, container runtime and version (containerd/docker), available disk on registry host
- Confirm hash of existing bundle: run sha256sum on current deployed images list and saved manifests
- Filesystem limits: ensure /var/lib/registry has >= estimated bundle size + 20% (see section: bundle sizing)
- Time sync: NTP/chrony reachable inside network or manually set and verify within 1s on nodes
- Backup: create etcd snapshot and store offline; export TF state (if using remote state, create presigned snapshot and store locally)
- Admin creds: ensure kubeconfig with cluster-admin and registry admin user available
- Controls: confirm maintenance window and rollback approval group.

Commands (examples):
- k8s version: kubectl version --short
- container runtime: ssh bastion 'crictl version || docker --version'
- etcd snapshot (k8s managed): kubectl -n kube-system exec -it etcd-0 -- etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db && scp to bastion

2) ARTIFACT CAPTURE & SIGNING (on internet-connected workstation)
Goal: produce a compact, signed bundle that can be transported into the air-gapped environment.
Steps:
- Generate image list from our release manifest: release-manifest.yaml -> images.txt (one image per line).
- Pull images and produce OCI layout (preferred) or docker tar: use Skopeo/crane to copy images into an OCI layout directory for efficient registry import.
  - sample: crane copy --format oci --insecure-policy --authfile ~/.docker/config.json image:tag oci-layout-dir/image:tag
- Save Helm charts and CRD manifests with versions pinned. Render templates for target k8s version (helm template --kube-version).
- Produce a top-level manifest.json with: images, chart versions, sha256 checksums, expected k8s api versions, minimum kernel/container runtime versions.
- Sign the manifest with cosign (or GPG if customer requires): cosign sign --key cosign.key manifest.json. Keep signature file next to bundle.
- Create tarball: tar czf redwood-offline-bundle-<version>-<date>.tgz oci-layout charts manifests manifest.json manifest.sig

Bundle sizing guidance:
- Typical medium deployment (base platform + models stripped): 6–12GB OCI layout.
- GPU-heavy models and large snapshot layers: can be 60–200GB.
- Compress and prune layers: remove dev/debug images from the release manifest to reduce size.

3) IMPORTING INTO OFFLINE REGISTRY (on bastion/registry host)
Options depend on target registry type: Harbor, ACR offline import, Artifactory, Nexus. We prefer OCI layout + registry import tools (oras/crane/skopeo).
- Example with skopeo for OCI layout: skopeo copy oci:./oci-layout docker://local-registry.internal:5000/repo --dest-tls-verify=false
- Example using crane to push images from a tar/oci layout: for image in $(cat images.txt); do crane push oci-layout/$image local-registry.internal:5000/$image; done
- For chartmuseum/helm: upload helm charts using curl or helm push plugin, then index.
- After import, run registry garbage-collect if supported (Harbor GC mode) and verify tags are present.

Verification commands (registry host):
- curl -k https://local-registry.internal:5000/v2/_catalog
- skopeo inspect docker://local-registry.internal:5000/repo/image:tag
- Check manifest signature: cosign verify --key cosign.pub manifest.json 

4) TERRAFORM NOTES & STATE MIGRATION (on bastion with access to infra tooling)
- Keep a trimmed TF module for airgap: remove remote provider plugins that require outbound access (or vendor them into the bundle). Use terraform init -plugin-dir to point to bundled providers.
- Backend: if remote backend (S3/GCS) is used by customers, create a one-time state export and sync to a local file backend for the duration of the airgap operation. Document step: terraform state pull > state-2025-02-*.backup
- Providers: include exact provider binaries (linux_amd64) in artifacts/providers/ and use "terraform init -plugin-dir=./providers".
- Example variable overrides: create a tfvars-airgap.hcl with registry endpoint overrides, skip_internet_checks = true, local_bundle_path = "/opt/redwood/bundles/"
- Idempotency note: scripts should run terraform plan -out=plan.bin and then terraform apply "plan.bin" to ensure deterministic changes.

5) UPGRADE STRATEGY (operator-first, control-plane guarded)
- Upgrade sequence recommendation (minimal blast radius):
  a) Control plane infra (TF changes that change LB/certs) in maintenance window with ops approval
  b) Operator binary and CRDs (apply CRDs first, wait 30s, then apply operator deployment)
  c) Platform core pods (auth, scheduler, sidecars) rolled with PodDisruptionBudgets honored
  d) Model-serving components and heavier GPU workloads last
- Canary pattern: apply operator to a single namespace or node pool first, monitor for 1–2h for errors and CPU/memory anomalies before expanding.
- Upgrade scripts should be dry-runable: ./upgrade-offline.sh --plan-only generates bundle checks and TF plan.

6) VERIFICATION SUITES (post-upgrade)
- Smoke tests: k8s API reachability, pod status, operator CR reconciliation, simple generate request that returns expected token counts.
- Performance sanity: run 50 short inference calls against an internal canary model, verify p50/p95 latency within agreed delta.
- Data-path tests: verify model snapshot mounts, KV cache behavior (if enabled), and streaming correctness.
- Security tests: verify certificate fingerprints and cosign signature presence.

Sample verification commands (scripts):
- kubectl -n redwood get po -o wide --show-labels
- curl -sS -k https://canary.local.redwood/api/v1/health | jq .status
- python tools/run_smoke.py --endpoint https://canary.local.redwood --apikey-file ~/.redwood/apikey

7) ROLLBACK PLAN
- Rollback trigger conditions: failed canary, >5% error rate on health endpoints, operator crashlooping > 3x in 10m, or critical TF change could not be applied cleanly.
- Rollback steps (fast):
  - Re-apply previous operator deployment manifest (kubectl apply -f operator-vX.Y.Z.yaml)
  - If TF changed critical infra, revert state using saved state backup: terraform state push state-YYYYMMDD.backup or restore S3 snapshot.
  - Re-import prior image tags into registry if overwritten (tags should be immutable; if overwritten, restore from bundle).
- Verify etcd snapshot recovery: etcdctl snapshot status /tmp/etcd-snap.db; restore into etcd cluster following k8s upstream restore guidance.

8) SMALL SCRIPTS & EXCERPTS (copy these into your bastion scripts dir)
- checksum-verify.sh
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  BUNDLE=$1
  cd /tmp/unpack || exit 2
  echo "Verifying manifest signature..."
  cosign verify --key /opt/keys/cosign.pub ${BUNDLE}/manifest.json || { echo "signature invalid"; exit 3; }
  while read -r f h; do
    echo "check $f -> $h"
    sha256sum -c <(echo "$h  $f") || { echo "checksum fail: $f"; exit 4; }
  done < ${BUNDLE}/checksums.txt

- import-oci.sh (sketch)
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  OCI_DIR=$1
  REG=$2 # local-registry:5000
  for img in $(cat ${OCI_DIR}/images.txt); do
    echo "pushing $img to $REG"
    crane push ${OCI_DIR}/$img ${REG}/$img || { echo "push failed $img"; exit 5; }
  done

9) KNOWN PITFALLS & OPERATOR NOTES
- Provider plugins: missing provider binary will cause terraform init to fail silently in airgap. Always ship provider binaries and test terraform init in an offline VM before creating bundle.
- CRD ordering: applying CRDs after operator will cause controller to reconcile with missing types; always apply CRDs first.
- Immutable tags: encourage customers to use immutable manifests or sha-digests. Tag re-use can cause silent drift and complicate rollbacks.
- Layer dedup: large model layers often duplicate across images; using OCI layout and content-addressable imports reduces transfer size.

10) OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve before final run)
- Should we include signed plugin provider binaries and how to handle licensing for third-party providers? (legal consult required)
- Best practice for TLS cert rotation during prolonged upgrade windows? Should certs be rotated pre- or post-upgrade?
- Does the customer want us to automate presigned state snapshots for remote backends or prefer manual state handoff?

11) NEXT ACTIONS (owner: Maya)
- Convert this playbook to a step-by-step checklist UI in Console runbook mode (task estimate: 3 days).
- Produce a golden test bundle (small footprint) and validate import against a seeded local Harbor instance (owner: Liam, target: 2025-02-01).
- Draft legal note for vendoring provider binaries and include in release notes (owner: Priya).

Appendix: quick reference commands
- cosign sign/verify: cosign sign --key cosign.key manifest.json ; cosign verify --key cosign.pub manifest.json
- save tf state: terraform state pull > state-backup.json
- import oci: skopeo copy oci:./layout docker://registry:5000/repo --dest-tls-verify=false
- basic smoke test: bash tools/smoke_canary.sh --endpoint https://canary.local

Contact notes:
- Slack: #private-deployments (triage channel)
- Oncall: eng-sre rotation list in CONF-8472

Status: working draft. This document will be converted to a step-by-step playbook and small CLI utilities that wrap the sample scripts above. Please add notes inline and link to any specific customer-run requirements under linked_artifacts.
